after.worked_solution:
To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the numbers to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x & <8 \\ {x}^{2}-2x-8 & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y={x}^{2}-2x-8$ lies below the $x$-axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x-8 & =0 \\ (x+2)(x-4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=-2$ and $x=4,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14029391/assets/83e87f616c1e9a74065016df2d6a0bbfac5bcdc8ee9326721b13a2bd8a8f16d4.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
{x}^{2}-2x-8<0,
$$

we look for the part of the parabola that is below the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $-2<x<4.$ 

Using interval notation, we write $x\in (-2,4).$

after.worked_solution:
To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the numbers to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3 & \ge 2{x}^{2} \\ -2{x}^{2}+x+3 & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y=-2{x}^{2}+x+3$ lies **above** the $x$-axis or touches this axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}+x+3 & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2}-x-3 & =0 \\ (2{x}^{2}-3x)+(2x-3) & =0 \\ x(2x-3)+(2x-3) & =0 \\ (x+1)(2x-3) & =0 \\ 2(x+1)(x-\frac{3}{2}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=-1$ and $x=\frac{3}{2},$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14029391/assets/86d7fbea75961bdb83c014ca9febb735e6a1745f71e8e094de416998b2072630.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
-2{x}^{2}+x+3\ge 0,
$$

 
we look for the part of the parabola that is **above** the $x$-axis or touches this axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $-1\le x\le \frac{3}{2}.$

Using interval notation, we write $x\in [-1,\frac{3}{2}].$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}+x+3 & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2}-x-3 & =0 \\ (2{x}^{2}-3x)+(2x-3) & =0 \\ x(2x-3)+(2x-3) & =0 \\ (x+1)(2x-3) & =0 \\ 2(x+1)(x-\frac{3}{2}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=-1$ and $x=\frac{3}{2},$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

Based on the graph, the solution is $-1\le x\le \frac{3}{2}.$
